children.title: First Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights
children.path: Meta Q1 2026 Exhibit 99.1.pdf/Root/First Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights
children.summary: This section presents a table of financial highlights for Meta Platforms, Inc. for the three months ended March 31, 2026, compared to the same period in 2025. Key metrics include Revenue ($56,311 million), Costs and expenses ($33,439 million), Income from operations ($22,872 million), Net income ($26,773 million), and Diluted earnings per share ($10.44). The table also details the effective tax rate and includes a footnote explaining significant tax benefits related to the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

children.title: First Quarter 2026 Operational and Other Financial Highlights
children.path: Meta Q1 2026 Exhibit 99.1.pdf/Root/First Quarter 2026 Operational and Other Financial Highlights
children.summary: This section details Meta's operational and financial performance for the first quarter of 2026. It reports that Family daily active people (DAP) reached an average of 3.56 billion, a 4% year-over-year increase, though noting declines in Iran and Russia. Ad impressions grew by 19%, while the average price per ad rose 12%. Total revenue was $56.31 billion (up 33%), with costs and expenses totaling $33.44 billion. The company also reported capital expenditures of $19.84 billion, cash flow from operating activities of $32.23 billion, free cash flow of $12.39 billion, and a headcount of 77,986.

children.title: CFO Outlook Commentary
children.summary: This page contains a CFO Outlook Commentary providing financial guidance for 2026. It details expected revenue ranges of $58-61 billion for the second quarter and total expenses between $162-169 billion for the full year. The text also outlines anticipated capital expenditures, tax rates, and mentions ongoing legal and regulatory headwinds in the EU and U.S.

children.title: Webcast and Conference Call Information
children.path: Meta Q1 2026 Exhibit 99.1.pdf/Root/Webcast and Conference Call Information
children.summary: This section provides details regarding a conference call hosted by Meta to discuss its results, scheduled for 2:30 p.m. PT / 5:30 p.m. ET. It specifies that the live webcast and subsequent replay will be available on the Meta Investor Relations website (investor.atmeta.com), along with earnings press releases, financial tables, slide presentations, and transcripts of analyst calls.

children.title: Disclosure Information
children.summary: This section outlines Meta's channels for disclosing material non-public information and complying with Regulation FD. These channels include the investor.atmeta.com and meta.com/news websites, as well as Mark Zuckerberg's social media profiles on Facebook, Instagram, and Threads.

children.title: About Meta
children.summary: This section describes Meta's mission to build the future of human connection using artificial intelligence and immersive technologies. It highlights the company's history starting with Facebook in 2004, mentions its apps like Messenger, Instagram, and WhatsApp, and states that Meta is moving beyond 2D screens to foster deeper connections.

children.title: Contacts
children.summary: The 'Contacts' section lists the designated points of contact for Meta, divided into two categories: Investors and Press. For investors, it provides the name Kenneth Dorell along with his email address (investor@meta.com) and website (investor.atmeta.com). For press inquiries, it lists Matt Tye with his email address (press@meta.com) and website (meta.com/news).

children.title: Forward-Looking Statements
children.summary: The section contains a standard legal disclaimer regarding forward-looking statements. It warns that the press release includes predictions about future business plans and expectations which may differ from actual results due to various factors such as macroeconomic conditions, geopolitical events, user retention, advertising revenue reliance, data signal dependency, product changes, AI initiatives, community growth focus, brand reputation, privacy/security efforts, competition, government actions, litigation, acquisitions, security breaches, operational scale, and market conditions. The text references specific filings (Form 10-K filed January 29, 2026, and Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2026) available on the SEC website and the company's Investor Relations site (investor.atmeta.com). It notes the press release date is April 29, 2026, and states the company undertakes no obligation to update these statements.

children.title: Non-GAAP Financial Measures
children.summary: This section explains the company's use of non-GAAP financial measures to supplement its GAAP financial statements. It details three specific measures: revenue excluding foreign exchange effect, advertising revenue excluding foreign exchange effect, and free cash flow. The text clarifies that these measures are intended to provide useful supplemental information for investors by enabling comparison of results between periods and offering greater transparency into key metrics used by management. It also describes the adjustments made to calculate these measures, such as translating revenue using prior year's exchange rates and subtracting purchases of property and equipment and principal payments on finance leases from free cash flow.

children.title: Segment Results
children.summary: This page presents the segment results for a company, detailing financial performance across two reportable segments: Family of Apps (FoA) and Reality Labs (RL). It includes a table titled 'Segment Information' that lists revenue and income from operations for the three months ended March 31, 2026, and 2025. The data is presented in millions and covers specific categories such as advertising, other revenue, and total revenue.

children.title: Reconciliation of GAAP to Non-GAAP Results
children.path: Meta Q1 2026 Exhibit 99.1.pdf/Root/Reconciliation of GAAP to Non-GAAP Results
children.summary: The page displays a financial table titled 'Reconciliation of GAAP to Non-GAAP Results' for the three months ended March 31, comparing data from 2026 and 2025. The table details revenue figures (total and advertising), year-over-year percentage changes, and cash flow metrics including net cash provided by operating activities and free cash flow.
